newsitem.title: LEBANON: Talks over formation of Lebanon cabinet drag on.
newsitem.headline: Talks over formation of Lebanon cabinet drag on.

text.p: Talks over the formation of a new Lebanese government dragged on as political leaders tried on Thursday to solve disputes over the distribution of cabinet posts.

Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri, who was renominated for a third term of office on October 24, met President Elias Hrawi at the presidential palace for nearly two hours to discuss ways to end the stalemate over the government's formation.
Syria, Lebanon's main power broker with 35,000 troops there, was also exerting efforts to end the deadlock.

Hariri was originally expected to form his cabinet at the end of last week but ran into difficulties, first with the Maronite Christian president -- which have since been resolved -- and now with Shi'ite Moslem Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri.
Official sources said Lebanon's ruling troika -- Hrawi, Berri and Hariri -- have been trying over the past few days to finalise distribution of key portfolios between the religious communities.
Under Lebanon's confessional power sharing system, the cabinet and parliament must be divided equally between Moslems and Christians.
Asked when the cabinet will be formed, Hariri told reporters after meeting Hrawi: "Soon, soon...Many things have been resolved and I think we're reaching an end (to the problems)."

The sources said the main bone of contention between Hariri and Berri is the Sunni Moslem premier's insistence to nominate to the cabinet a Shi'ite MP close to him. In return, Berri demands his allies control more than one key portfolio.
They said the head of Syrian army intelligence in Lebanon Major General Ghazi Kenaan met Berri on Wednesday night in a bid to defuse the rift.
Kenaan's talks with Berri followed talks between Hariri and Syrian President Hafez al-Assad in Damascus on Tuesday that touched on the shape of the government.
